fix: In 'X brown with a blackish wavy pattern' the colour after 'with a ... pattern/markings/spots' belongs to the marking, not to the whole part. Don't annotate it as the part's colour, or give it a pattern/marking context slot.
reason: The achene is brown. Only the wavy pattern on it is blackish, so 'fruit colour black' misstates the achene's colour.
'Shrubs, 10–20(–50) dm' is plant height. Converting to 100–200 cm with a 500 cm extreme is right.
'blue-purple or blue' is read correctly as two alternatives: purplish blue and blue.
The margins are said to be not dentate. The few shallow teeth mentioned after are serrate, which is consistent with that. Putting the margin quality on the lamina follows the usual pattern.

fix: In a run of corolla descriptions ('lobes ..., plicae ..., lanceolate-ovate, entire, acute-acuminate'), the trailing adjectives belong to the nearest preceding noun (plicae), not to a default 'leaf'.
reason: 'acute-acuminate' describes the corolla plicae, right before the stamens. It does not describe leaves.
'Rhizomes blackish' gives colour black with 'approximately', which is right.
The bracts are smaller than the calyx lobes. Decreased size with the calyx lobe (FLOPO_0986005) as the comparison part is right.
The leaf apex runs from acute to shortly acuminate. The range is captured with 'shortly' as a degree word.
'Leaves surpassing culm' means the leaves are longer than the culm. Culm is a synonym of stem (PO_0009047).
'Flaccid' primary leaves means limp. 'Flexible' is the closest existing PATO term. It only covers the primary leaves, but there is no slot for that here.
'Thorns & Spines: Absent' is read correctly as thorns absent.
The leaf sheaths are usually shorter than the internodes. Comparison part and 'usually' are both right.
The panicle is 1½ inches across, which is 3.81 cm wide.
'Seeds numerous' is read correctly as seeds present, many.

fix: A hyphenated pair like 'apiculate-obtuse' is one compound value (obtuse with a small point). Don't split it so that only 'apiculate' becomes the second alternative, and never use the attribute 'sharpness' (PATO_0000944) as a value.
reason: The second alternative is 'apiculate-obtuse', but it was cut down to 'apiculate' and mapped to the attribute 'sharpness', which is not a value.
Corolla white to lavender. Mapping lavender to violet (FLOPO_0988027) is acceptable.
2–4 secondary veins on each side of the midrib (PO_0020139), inside the lamina, is right.

fix: In 'the lobes 14–15 mm long, 7–8 mm wide, planar at anthesis', the adjectives still describe the lobes named earlier in the run, not the corolla as a whole.
reason: It is the corolla lobes that are planar at anthesis. The corolla itself is lobed 3/4 of the way down.

fix: 'pubescent along veins' limits the hairs to the veins. The position slot must record it, or the annotation says the whole lower surface is hairy.
reason: The underside is hairy only along the veins. Without that limit the annotation overstates the hair cover.
'± spathulate' stigmas gives spatulate with 'approximately', which is right.
The blade is about 9 × 4 cm, so a width of 4 cm is right. The 'ca.' could be kept as 'approximately', but the value is correct.
Bracts persistent in fruit gives non-deciduous with the fruit stage, which is right.
The keel petal is rounded at the apex. Petal apex as bearer with obtuse is acceptable.
Capsule obovoid-ellipsoid is read correctly as a range of shapes.

fix: When a list switches to sub-parts ('margins ..., medians ..., apices ...'), the quality belongs to that sub-part, not to the whole phyllary.
reason: Only the phyllary tips turn brown with age. The sides are yellowish white and the middles green.

fix: 'Male/female raceme' must fill the sex slot. In monoecious or dioecious taxa the length is false for the female inflorescence.
reason: 17–30 cm is the male raceme only. The plant is monoecious.
Capsule from ovoid-globose to globose is read as ovoid to globose, an acceptable simplification.

fix: In 'with ... ferruginous hairs beneath', the colour word describes the hairs, not the leaf.
reason: The rusty colour is the colour of the hairs on the leaf underside. The leaf is not orange.
Upper (adaxial) surface glabrous, which is right.
7–13 secondary veins on each side of the midvein, which is right.
